newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sees annual oil income $2 billion over budget.
newsitem.headline: Iran sees annual oil income $2 billion over budget.

text.p: Iran expects revenue from oil exports to exceed budget forecasts by more than $2 billion, Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said on Friday.
Aghazadeh told Iran's news agency IRNA that oil income was expected to reach above $18 billion, more than $2 billion over budget estimates for the Iranian year ending on March 20 1997.
The budget envisaged petroleum earnings of $15.99 billion, based on exports of 2.6 million barrels per day of crude oil at $15.5 a barrel.
Iranian television said last month Iran's crude oil had been sold at an average $17.8 per barrel in the current year.
Iran, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, is the world's third largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway.
